identification: Three Australian George V silver (.925) florins dated 1926, 1927 and 1928 in hand-labelled card holders (grades pencilled 4, 5 and 6). Obverses noted as 6 clear pearls with centre diamond (the scarcer/ordinary headband varieties are not distinguished by this). Look about VF, some wear. Oddity: the holder labelled 1927 appears to show the coat of arms reverse, but the only 1927 florin is the Canberra Parliament House type, so the date label may be wrong (could be another date) and must be checked.

searches_tried: pipeline/comps.py: 'florin 1926', 'florin 1927', 'florin 1928', 'george florin'; work/comps.py: 'florin 1926', 'florin george' (no resale comps found). No single-coin 1926/1928 hits; only multi-coin Noble and Leski lots. No Armitage or Gowans same-item hits seen.
chrome_hint: eBay AU sold/Terapeak: 'australian florin 1926', 'australian florin 1928', 'florin 1927 coat of arms' (to settle the date), each with Sold Items filter, last 12 months, grade VF. Noble Numismatics lot search for 'florin 1926' and 'florin 1928' singles; Downies and Status International results for 'florin 1926 VF'. Check coin-dealer retail (Perth Mint dealers, Coins of Oz) as ASKING for 1926 and 1928 VF. Silver content approx 11.3 g .925 each, melt roughly $12-18 per coin at current silver.
viewing_check: Read each date with a loupe, especially the 1927 (confirm reverse is Parliament House Canberra type or not; coat of arms with 1927 would be odd). Photograph the date and reverse of each coin. Check for cleaning, scratches and rim knocks; confirm real grade (VF vs F) and that none are lead or copy forgeries. Check 1926 and 1928 more closely as they are the scarcer dates in better grade.
